headline: Co-op Legal Services is using AI to score staff phone calls with customers seeking advice on wills and estates, a whistleblower says.
score_reason: Pool 6; read in full; event 8 Oct 2026; account rests on a whistleblower and staff, with the company replying, so no raise or lowering.
importance_line: AI scoring of routine customer calls is reaching legal services, which affects staff first and then customers and employers, and the doubt is that the account rests on anonymous staff and the company's own statements.
summary: The Guardian reports that Co-op Legal Services, part of the Co-op group, which also runs supermarkets, undertakers and insurance, records and analyses calls between its advisers and customers, using an AI model trained to check more than 50 aspects of each call and give managers pass or fail scores. A whistleblower calls the system oppressive, while the Co-op says the AI is a support tool and not a decision-maker.
notes: Full text read (fulltext C14-05, Guardian HTTP 200). Company statements and a union statement are included. Pool curator note: jobs and labor.
